quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.text: Two kinds of animal do not corrupt the water they die in: those with {{c1::no flowing blood}} — a fly, a scorpion — and those that {{c2::live in water, born in it and staying in it}} — a fish, a frog

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Why does an animal with no flowing blood not make water impure by dying in it?
quduri.back: Because it is the blood that makes a carcass impure

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.meaning: carrion — an animal that died without being slaughtered

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Which parts of a <bdi>مَيْتَة</bdi> are pure?

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Water used to be stored in leather. What makes an animal hide pure?

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Which two hides does tanning not purify?
quduri.back: The pig's and the human being's

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Why are the rulings of wells still studied?
quduri.back: For the principles behind them — and some places in the world still rely on wells

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: How is a well purified when impurity falls into it?
quduri.back: By drawing its water out — <bdi>نَزْح</bdi>; removing the water in it is what purifies it

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: What kind of well does drawing out all its water (<bdi>نَزْح</bdi>) assume?
quduri.back: One not fed by a spring — essentially a storage hole in the ground

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.text: An animal falls into a well and dies. If it is small — a mouse, a small bird, a gecko — {{c1::20 to 30}} buckets are drawn out, by the bucket's size; if medium — a chicken, a cat — {{c2::40 to 50}}; if large — a human, a sheep, a dog — {{c3::all the water}}

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Whatever the size of the animal that died in a well, when is all its water drawn out?
quduri.back: When the animal has bloated or started to come apart

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: How is a spring-fed well, which cannot be emptied, purified?
quduri.back: By drawing out about as much water as it held

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: How much did Muḥammad al-Shaybānī say to draw from a spring-fed well, and on what did he base it?
quduri.back: 200 to 300 buckets — from the wells he saw in Baghdad

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.text: For Abū Ḥanīfah, if a dead animal is found in a well and no one knows when it fell in, those who made wuḍūʾ from it repeat {{c1::one day and night}} of prayers if it has not bloated, and {{c2::three days and nights}} if it has bloated or come apart

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Besides repeating prayers, what must be done when a well whose water was used turns out to hold a dead animal?
quduri.back: Everything its water touched must be purified

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: What do Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad hold about repeating prayers when a dead animal is found in a well and no one knows when it fell in?
quduri.back: Nothing need be repeated until it is established when it fell in

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.meaning: leftover drinking water — what is left in a container after someone drinks from it

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: What general rule decides whether an animal's <bdi>سُؤْر</bdi> is pure?
quduri.back: Whether its meat is ḥalāl to eat: if it is, its saliva — and so its suʾr — is pure; if not, impure

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.text: Rulings on <bdi>سُؤْر</bdi>: {{c1::pure — <bdi>طَاهِر</bdi>}} for humans and animals ḥalāl to eat; {{c2::impure — <bdi>نَجِس</bdi>}} for animals that are not, such as the dog, the pig and beasts of prey; {{c3::disliked — <bdi>مَكْرُوه</bdi>}} for animals that commonly live in houses, such as the cat; {{c4::doubtful — <bdi>مَشْكُوك فِيهِ</bdi>}} for the donkey and the mule

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Water a cat has drunk from is at hand, and so is other water. Which is better to use?
quduri.back: The other water — a house animal's suʾr is disliked, though usable

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Why is the <bdi>سُؤْر</bdi> of the donkey and the mule doubtful?

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: assorted points, wells, suʾr — class notes 2026-10-07
quduri.front: If the only water available is a donkey's or a mule's <bdi>سُؤْر</bdi>, what should one do?
quduri.back: Make wuḍūʾ with it, and also make tayammum

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which saying of the Prophet ﷺ makes a person's ending decisive for their deeds?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: “Actions are judged by their endings” — <bdi>إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالخَوَاتِيمِ</bdi> (al-Bukhārī)
